Claude Code applies the cap itself before each request, so it holds on every provider, including Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry. Requires Claude Code v2.1.267 or later.
description.zh: Cap the effort level a session can use, leaving lower levels available. Any higher level runs at the cap instead, including one from /effort, the /model picker, --effort, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, a skill's or subagent's effort frontmatter, or the model's own default. Claude Code applies the cap itself before each request, so it holds on every provider, including Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry. Requires Claude Code v2.1.267 or later.

settings.type: number of terminal columns, a whole number, minimum 40. Claude Code ignores any other value
settings.default: unset, so prose wraps at the terminal edge

description.en: Cap the width of the prose in Claude's responses so lines stay readable in a wide terminal. Paragraphs, headings, lists, and blockquotes wrap within this many columns, while tables and code blocks keep the full terminal width. Requires Claude Code v2.1.282 or later.
description.zh: Cap the width of the prose in Claude's responses so lines stay readable in a wide terminal. Paragraphs, headings, lists, and blockquotes wrap within this many columns, while tables and code blocks keep the full terminal width. Requires Claude Code v2.1.282 or later.

settings.scope: Any file. Set it in managed settings to pin an organization-wide minimum that user and project settings can't lower.
settings.type: string, a version number such as "2.1.100"; a value that isn't a valid version is ignored
settings.default: unset, so updates can install any version the channel offers

description.en: Keep background auto-updates and claude update from installing any version below this one, so moving to the "stable" channel doesn't downgrade you from a newer "latest" build. Claude Code writes this key for you when you choose to stay on your current version while switching channels in /config, and clears it when you switch back to "latest".
description.zh: Keep background auto-updates and claude update from installing any version below this one, so moving to the "stable" channel doesn't downgrade you from a newer "latest" build. Claude Code writes this key for you when you choose to stay on your current version while switching channels in /config, and clears it when you switch back to "latest".

settings.type: string, a model alias or full model ID
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses your account's default model

description.en: Set the model every new session uses, so you don't have to pick one with /model each time. Setting it here doesn't stop you from switching mid-session. If your admin set an organization default model to override user selection, you get that model even when you set this key in user, project, or local settings.
description.zh: Set the model every new session uses, so you don't have to pick one with /model each time. Setting it here doesn't stop you from switching mid-session. If your admin set an organization default model to override user selection, you get that model even when you set this key in user, project, or local settings.

settings.type: object mapping model ID to provider model ID
settings.default: unset

description.en: Map Anthropic model IDs to provider-specific model IDs, such as Amazon Bedrock inference profile ARNs. Each model picker entry then uses its mapped value when calling the provider API. Administrators use this on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry to route each model version to a specific inference profile, version name, or deployment for governance, cost allocation, or regional routing.
description.zh: Map Anthropic model IDs to provider-specific model IDs, such as Amazon Bedrock inference profile ARNs. Each model picker entry then uses its mapped value when calling the provider API. Administrators use this on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry to route each model version to a specific inference profile, version name, or deployment for governance, cost allocation, or regional routing.

settings.scope: User or managed. Claude Code reads the key from managed settings, --settings, and user settings, and ignores it in project and local settings so a repository you clone can't relabel the picker. The highest of those three that sets the key supplies the whole lineup, and Claude Code never combines lineups from two sources.
settings.type: object with an options array of rows and an optional replaceBuiltInOptions Boolean
settings.default: unset, so the picker shows the built-in lineup

description.en: List the models the /model picker offers, in the order you write them and under labels you choose, so the picker lists the models your organization runs, after the built-in lineup or instead of it. Each row's model is taken verbatim, so it accepts anything --model accepts: an alias such as opus, an Anthropic model ID, or a provider-format ID for Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or an LLM gateway. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
description.zh: List the models the /model picker offers, in the order you write them and under labels you choose, so the picker lists the models your organization runs, after the built-in lineup or instead of it. Each row's model is taken verbatim, so it accepts anything --model accepts: an alias such as opus, an Anthropic model ID, or a provider-format ID for Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or an LLM gateway. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

settings.scope: Managed. Deploy the key through server-managed settings, an MDM policy, a managed-settings.json file, or a policy helper. Claude Code ignores it in user, project, and local settings, in --settings, and on Windows in the user-writable HKCU registry. With server-managed settings, each session reports costs at list price until that session's settings fetch has confirmed the setting. A host application that embeds Claude Code and sets CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST can supply a table of its own through the SDK managedSettings option, which Claude Code uses only when no managed source sets the key and only in Claude Code v2.1.246 or later.
settings.type: object with an optional multiplier and an optional overrides map
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code reports list price unless a host application supplies a table

description.en: Report spend at the rates your organization pays instead of list price. Set it when your organization has contracted rates, so the dollar figures developers see match your bill. Claude Code applies the rates in /usage, the status line, the Agent SDK's total_cost_usd, the --max-budget-usd limit, and the OpenTelemetry cost metric and events. You supply the rates: Claude Code doesn't read them from your contract or the Claude Console. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
description.zh: Report spend at the rates your organization pays instead of list price. Set it when your organization has contracted rates, so the dollar figures developers see match your bill. Claude Code applies the rates in /usage, the status line, the Agent SDK's total_cost_usd, the --max-budget-usd limit, and the OpenTelemetry cost metric and events. You supply the rates: Claude Code doesn't read them from your contract or the Claude Console. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

settings.type: object mapping a model name to an object with any of these fields:
settings.default: unset

description.en: Save an effort level for each model you use. Requires Claude Code v2.1.251 or later.
description.zh: Save an effort level for each model you use. Requires Claude Code v2.1.251 or later.

settings.type: string, an executable path or a shell command line
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code adds no helper-generated headers

description.en: Run your own command to generate the headers Claude Code sends with OpenTelemetry exports, for backends whose tokens rotate. Claude Code runs it at startup and periodically after that, and expects a JSON object of string header values on stdout.
description.zh: Run your own command to generate the headers Claude Code sends with OpenTelemetry exports, for backends whose tokens rotate. Claude Code runs it at startup and periodically after that, and expects a JSON object of string header values on stdout.

settings.type: string, the name of a built-in or custom output style
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the default style

description.en: Select an output style by name. An output style is a saved set of instructions that changes Claude's role, tone, and output format, such as the built-in Explanatory and Learning styles or one you wrote yourself.
description.zh: Select an output style by name. An output style is a saved set of instructions that changes Claude's role, tone, and output format, such as the built-in Explanatory and Learning styles or one you wrote yourself.

settings.scope: Managed. Claude Code reads it from the highest-priority admin-controlled managed source.
settings.default: "first-wins"

description.en: Choose whether Claude Code applies managed settings supplied by an embedding host process, such as the Agent SDK or an IDE extension, when an admin-deployed managed tier is also present. With "first-wins", Claude Code drops the host-supplied settings; with "merge", it applies them under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter. Set "merge" when a host needs to pass its own restrictions to the sessions it launches, for example Claude Desktop delivering a gateway's egress allowlist.
description.zh: Choose whether Claude Code applies managed settings supplied by an embedding host process, such as the Agent SDK or an IDE extension, when an admin-deployed managed tier is also present. With "first-wins", Claude Code drops the host-supplied settings; with "merge", it applies them under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter. Set "merge" when a host needs to pass its own restrictions to the sessions it launches, for example Claude Desktop delivering a gateway's egress allowlist.

settings.type: object with allow, ask, deny, additionalDirectories, blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories, defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode, and disableAutoMode
settings.default: unset

description.en: Control which tools Claude can use without asking, which ones always prompt, and which ones are blocked, and set the permission mode a session starts in. Every permissions.* key below nests under this object.
description.zh: Control which tools Claude can use without asking, which ones always prompt, and which ones are blocked, and set the permission mode a session starts in. Every permissions.* key below nests under this object.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on the sandbox write access that project and local entries give
settings.default: unset

description.en: Give Claude file access to directories outside the one you started in, as additional working directories. Most .claude/ configuration is not discovered from these directories.
description.zh: Give Claude file access to directories outside the one you started in, as additional working directories. Most .claude/ configuration is not discovered from these directories.

settings.default: unset

description.en: List the tool uses Claude Code approves without asking you. In an MCP rule, can appear only in the tool name after the mcp____ prefix, such as mcp__github__get_; it can't appear in the server name.
description.zh: List the tool uses Claude Code approves without asking you. In an MCP rule, can appear only in the tool name after the mcp____ prefix, such as mcp__github__get_; it can't appear in the server name.

settings.default: unset

description.en: List the tool uses that prompt you for confirmation even in a permission mode that would otherwise approve them, such as acceptEdits or bypassPermissions. In dontAsk mode Claude Code denies a matching tool use instead of prompting.
description.zh: List the tool uses that prompt you for confirmation even in a permission mode that would otherwise approve them, such as acceptEdits or bypassPermissions. In dontAsk mode Claude Code denies a matching tool use instead of prompting.

settings.scope: Any file. A true in any file applies, so a repository can turn the block on for itself but can't lift yours.
settings.default: unset, so reads outside the working directories follow your permission mode

description.en: Make Claude's file tools refuse reads outside your working directories in every permission mode, including bypassPermissions. Claude Code denies Read, Grep, Glob, and LSP calls on those paths and tells Claude to ask you to add the directory with /add-dir. Files Claude Code itself needs stay readable, such as your skills, plugins, rules, agents, commands, and the CLAUDE.md memory file under ~/.claude/. Requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.
description.zh: Make Claude's file tools refuse reads outside your working directories in every permission mode, including bypassPermissions. Claude Code denies Read, Grep, Glob, and LSP calls on those paths and tells Claude to ask you to add the directory with /add-dir. Files Claude Code itself needs stay readable, such as your skills, plugins, rules, agents, commands, and the CLAUDE.md memory file under ~/.claude/. Requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.

settings.scope: Any file. auto and bypassPermissions don't take effect from project or local settings, so set them in ~/.claude/settings.json instead. Before v2.1.257, bypassPermissions took effect from any file. For conversations the VS Code extension starts, Claude Code reads only user, managed, and --settings values.
settings.default: unset

description.en: Set the permission mode new sessions start in. When you leave it unset, sessions start in the built-in default for your surface.
description.zh: Set the permission mode new sessions start in. When you leave it unset, sessions start in the built-in default for your surface.

settings.default: unset

description.en: List the tool uses Claude Code blocks. Use it for files that hold API keys, secrets, or environment values: Claude Code excludes matching files from file discovery and search results, denies reads of them, and blocks the Edit and Write tools on the matching paths.
description.zh: List the tool uses Claude Code blocks. Use it for files that hold API keys, secrets, or environment values: Claude Code excludes matching files from file discovery and search results, denies reads of them, and blocks the Edit and Write tools on the matching paths.

settings.scope: Any file. Typically set in managed settings to enforce organizational policy.
settings.default: unset

description.en: Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode. Claude Code then rejects the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag, and ignores an agent definition's permissionMode: bypassPermissions, so the subagent runs with the parent session's permission mode.
description.zh: Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode. Claude Code then rejects the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag, and ignores an agent definition's permissionMode: bypassPermissions, so the subagent runs with the parent session's permission mode.

settings.type: string, a path relative to the project root
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses ~/.claude/plans

description.en: Choose where Claude Code stores the plan files it writes in plan mode. Claude Code resolves the path relative to the project root.
description.zh: Choose where Claude Code stores the plan files it writes in plan mode. Claude Code resolves the path relative to the project root.

settings.type: object mapping a plugin ID to an object with an options field, mapping each option name to a string, number, Boolean, or array of strings, and an optional mcpServers field holding per-server user configuration values in the same shape
settings.default: unset

description.en: Store the non-sensitive answers you give a plugin's userConfig configuration dialog, keyed by plugin ID. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you fill in the dialog, so you don't need to edit it by hand. Claude Code stores sensitive options in the macOS Keychain instead, falling back to ~/.claude/.credentials.json when the Keychain rejects the write; on platforms without a supported keychain, it stores them in ~/.claude/.credentials.json.
description.zh: Store the non-sensitive answers you give a plugin's userConfig configuration dialog, keyed by plugin ID. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you fill in the dialog, so you don't need to edit it by hand. Claude Code stores sensitive options in the macOS Keychain instead, falling back to ~/.claude/.credentials.json when the Keychain rejects the write; on platforms without a supported keychain, it stores them in ~/.claude/.credentials.json.

settings.default: unset, so no marketplace-declared suggestions surface

description.en: Name the marketplaces whose plugins can appear as contextual install suggestions, in spinner tips and pinned at the top of the /plugin Discover tab. The built-in first-party frontend-design tip is unaffected. Suggestions come from each plugin's relevance declaration in its marketplace entry.
description.zh: Name the marketplaces whose plugins can appear as contextual install suggestions, in spinner tips and pinned at the top of the /plugin Discover tab. The built-in first-party frontend-design tip is unaffected. Suggestions come from each plugin's relevance declaration in its marketplace entry.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code shows the standard warning alone

description.en: Add your organization's own text to the plugin trust warning Claude Code shows before installation, for example to confirm that plugins from your internal marketplace are vetted.
description.zh: Add your organization's own text to the plugin trust warning Claude Code shows before installation, for example to confirm that plugins from your internal marketplace are vetted.

settings.scope: Managed. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file. Claude Code reads the key from the highest-priority managed source that carries a policy key and runs the helper only when that source is one of those three; it ignores the key in server-managed settings, the HKCU registry, and host-supplied parent settings.
settings.type: object with path, timeoutMs, and refreshIntervalMs
settings.default: unset, so no helper runs

description.en: Run an executable you deploy that computes managed settings at startup, so you can derive policy from device posture, identity, or a remote service instead of a static file. Claude Code runs the helper before it accepts the first prompt and treats the settings it emits as the managed settings for the session.
description.zh: Run an executable you deploy that computes managed settings at startup, so you can derive policy from device posture, identity, or a remote service instead of a static file. Claude Code runs the helper before it accepts the first prompt and treats the settings it emits as the managed settings for the session.

settings.scope: Managed. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever policyHelper is read.
settings.type: string, an absolute path in normalized form, without . or .. segments; on Windows, a drive-letter or UNC path that ends in .exe
settings.default: none; required when policyHelper is set

description.en: Name the helper executable Claude Code runs. For what happens when the path breaks the rules below, see Helper failures.
description.zh: Name the helper executable Claude Code runs. For what happens when the path breaks the rules below, see Helper failures.

settings.scope: Managed. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever policyHelper is read.
settings.type: integer, milliseconds: 0 to disable refresh, otherwise at least 60000
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code runs the helper once at startup

description.en: Have Claude Code re-run the helper in the background on an interval so policy changes reach a running session. When a refresh succeeds, its output replaces the previous managed settings without a restart; when a refresh fails, Claude Code keeps the policy it already has.
description.zh: Have Claude Code re-run the helper in the background on an interval so policy changes reach a running session. When a refresh succeeds, its output replaces the previous managed settings without a restart; when a refresh fails, Claude Code keeps the policy it already has.

settings.scope: Managed. Read from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry, or the managed settings file, wherever policyHelper is read.

description.en: Set how long Claude Code waits for the helper before treating the run as failed. A timed-out run fails the same way as a non-zero exit, so at startup Claude Code refuses to start.
description.zh: Set how long Claude Code waits for the helper before treating the run as failed. A timed-out run fails the same way as a non-zero exit, so at startup Claude Code refuses to start.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code also reads a value left in ~/.claude.json by older versions.
settings.default: "auto"

description.en: Choose how Claude Code notifies you when a task completes or a permission prompt is waiting. Appears in /config as Local notifications.
description.zh: Choose how Claude Code notifies you when a task completes or a permission prompt is waiting. Appears in /config as Local notifications.

settings.default: false

description.en: Reduce or turn off interface animations such as the spinner, shimmer, and flash effects. Appears in /config as Reduce motion.
description.zh: Reduce or turn off interface animations such as the spinner, shimmer, and flash effects. Appears in /config as Reduce motion.

settings.scope: User or managed. Claude Code reads the key from managed settings. It reads the key from user settings only on a machine with no managed settings, for a user who isn't signed in with a Team or Enterprise plan. It ignores the key in project and local settings and in a --settings file.
settings.default: unset

description.en: List the managed plugins whose mods run before every mod a user installs, in the listed order. When you set this key in managed settings, name sec-default@builtin in the list to keep the built-in guard. In managed settings, Claude Code skips an id whose plugin doesn't count as your organization's. See Install your organization's mods and set the order for those conditions and for how the two ordering keys work together.
description.zh: List the managed plugins whose mods run before every mod a user installs, in the listed order. When you set this key in managed settings, name sec-default@builtin in the list to keep the built-in guard. In managed settings, Claude Code skips an id whose plugin doesn't count as your organization's. See Install your organization's mods and set the order for those conditions and for how the two ordering keys work together.

settings.type: string, the launcher command as an argv prefix, such as an absolute path with optional arguments
settings.default: unset, so background processes start unwrapped

description.en: On macOS and Linux, place a corporate launcher command in front of the background processes Claude Code starts. Claude Code runs the launcher with its own command line appended, so the launcher must exec into Claude Code; see Run Claude Code behind a corporate launcher for the launcher contract. Requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later.
description.zh: On macOS and Linux, place a corporate launcher command in front of the background processes Claude Code starts. Claude Code runs the launcher with its own command line appended, so the launcher must exec into Claude Code; see Run Claude Code behind a corporate launcher for the launcher contract. Requires Claude Code v2.1.210 or later.

settings.default: unset, so each main-conversation request gets its default lifetime

description.en: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the main conversation. This key applies to your interactive, -p, and Agent SDK turns, together with the helpers Claude Code runs inline with them. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
description.zh: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the main conversation. This key applies to your interactive, -p, and Agent SDK turns, together with the helpers Claude Code runs inline with them. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

settings.default: true

description.en: Show or hide prompt suggestions, the grayed-out predictions that appear in your prompt input. Set it to false, or turn off Prompt suggestions in /config, to hide them.
description.zh: Show or hide prompt suggestions, the grayed-out predictions that appear in your prompt input. Set it to false, or turn off Prompt suggestions in /config, to hide them.

settings.type: string, a URL template using any of the five placeholders
settings.default: unset

description.en: Point the PR links Claude Code renders, in the footer badge and in tool-result summaries, at an internal code-review tool instead of github.com. Claude Code substitutes {host}, {owner}, {repo}, {number}, and {url} from the PR URL. GitLab merge request links on both surfaces keep their GitLab URL.
description.zh: Point the PR links Claude Code renders, in the footer badge and in tool-result summaries, at an internal code-review tool instead of github.com. Claude Code substitutes {host}, {owner}, {repo}, {number}, and {url} from the PR URL. GitLab merge request links on both surfaces keep their GitLab URL.

settings.scope: Any file. For a self-hosted environment ID, user or managed settings, or the --settings flag only.
settings.type: string, an environment ID such as env_... or ccpool_...
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the Anthropic-hosted environment when your list has one, and otherwise the first environment in your list that isn't a Remote Control bridge environment, or the first environment when every one is a bridge environment

description.en: Pick the default cloud environment for cloud sessions you create from the CLI, such as with claude --cloud. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you pick an environment with /remote-env.
description.zh: Pick the default cloud environment for cloud sessions you create from the CLI, such as with claude --cloud. Claude Code writes this key to your user settings when you pick an environment with /remote-env.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code also reads a value left in ~/.claude.json by older versions.
settings.default: unset, so the auto-connect default applies

description.en: Connect Remote Control automatically when each interactive session starts, instead of waiting for /remote-control. Set it to true to turn auto-connect on, false to turn it off. Appears in /config as Enable Remote Control for all sessions.
description.zh: Connect Remote Control automatically when each interactive session starts, instead of waiting for /remote-control. Set it to true to turn auto-connect on, false to turn it off. Appears in /config as Enable Remote Control for all sessions.

settings.scope: Managed. Claude Code gives no warning when it ignores the key elsewhere.
settings.type: string, a version number such as "2.1.150"; a value that isn't a valid version is ignored
settings.default: unset, so no ceiling applies

description.en: Set the newest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is newer, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to install an approved version through your organization's approved method; claude install may also work. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.
description.zh: Set the newest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is newer, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to install an approved version through your organization's approved method; claude install may also work. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.

settings.scope: Managed. Claude Code gives no warning when it ignores the key elsewhere.
settings.type: string, a version number such as "2.1.150"; a value that isn't a valid version is ignored
settings.default: unset, so no floor applies

description.en: Set the oldest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is older, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to update through your organization's approved method. The check runs at startup only, so a session that's already running continues. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.
description.zh: Set the oldest Claude Code version your organization allows to start. When the running version is older, Claude Code exits at startup and tells the user to update through your organization's approved method. The check runs at startup only, so a session that's already running continues. Requires Claude Code v2.1.163 or later.

settings.scope: Any file. When no settings file sets it, Claude Code falls back to respectGitignore in ~/.claude.json, which the /config toggle writes.
settings.default: true

description.en: Control whether the @ file picker leaves out files that match .gitignore patterns. Appears in /config as Respect .gitignore in file picker.
description.zh: Control whether the @ file picker leaves out files that match .gitignore patterns. Appears in /config as Respect .gitignore in file picker.

settings.default: true

description.en: Choose whether Claude responds after you run a shell command with the ! prefix in the input box. By default, Claude Code adds the command's output to the conversation and Claude replies to it. Set this key to false to add the output to context without a reply, so you can run several commands and ask about them together.
description.zh: Choose whether Claude responds after you run a shell command with the ! prefix in the input box. By default, Claude Code adds the command's output to the conversation and Claude replies to it. Set this key to false to add the output to context without a reply, so you can run several commands and ask about them together.

settings.type: object with enabled, failIfUnavailable, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, excludedCommands, allowUnsandboxedCommands, enableWeakerNestedSandbox, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation, allowAppleEvents, bwrapPath, socatPath, ignoreViolations, and ripgrep, plus the filesystem, network, and credentials objects
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code runs commands without a sandbox

description.en: Isolate the Bash commands Claude runs from your filesystem and network with sandboxing. Turn the sandbox on with enabled, then narrow or widen what sandboxed commands can touch with the filesystem, network, and credentials sub-objects. The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2.
description.zh: Isolate the Bash commands Claude runs from your filesystem and network with sandboxing. Turn the sandbox on with enabled, then narrow or widen what sandboxed commands can touch with the filesystem, network, and credentials sub-objects. The sandbox runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2.

settings.default: false

description.en: Let sandboxed commands on macOS send Apple Events, which open, osascript, and tools that open URLs in a browser need; without it they fail with error -600. This removes code-execution isolation: sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt, and can send AppleScript commands to running applications such as Terminal, subject to the per-app macOS automation-consent prompt (TCC).
description.zh: Let sandboxed commands on macOS send Apple Events, which open, osascript, and tools that open URLs in a browser need; without it they fail with error -600. This removes code-execution isolation: sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt, and can send AppleScript commands to running applications such as Terminal, subject to the per-app macOS automation-consent prompt (TCC).

settings.scope: Any file, with a limit on project and local settings
settings.default: true

description.en: Let Claude retry a command outside the sandbox with the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter after the sandbox blocks it. When it's false, Claude Code ignores that parameter. While the sandbox is running, commands Claude runs are then sandboxed unless they match an excludedCommands entry. The /sandbox Overrides tab shows that state as Strict sandbox mode. A false in managed settings turns on strict sandbox mode for the developers it covers.
description.zh: Let Claude retry a command outside the sandbox with the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter after the sandbox blocks it. When it's false, Claude Code ignores that parameter. While the sandbox is running, commands Claude runs are then sandboxed unless they match an excludedCommands entry. The /sandbox Overrides tab shows that state as Strict sandbox mode. A false in managed settings turns on strict sandbox mode for the developers it covers.

settings.default: true

description.en: Let Claude Code run sandboxed Bash commands without a permission prompt. Commands that can't run in the sandbox still go through the regular permission flow, and deny rules and content-scoped ask rules such as Bash(git push *) still apply; a bare Bash ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands. Set it to false to send sandboxed commands through the regular permission flow too, which the /sandbox Mode tab calls regular permissions mode.
description.zh: Let Claude Code run sandboxed Bash commands without a permission prompt. Commands that can't run in the sandbox still go through the regular permission flow, and deny rules and content-scoped ask rules such as Bash(git push *) still apply; a bare Bash ask rule is skipped for sandboxed commands. Set it to false to send sandboxed commands through the regular permission flow too, which the /sandbox Mode tab calls regular permissions mode.

settings.scope: Managed. Claude Code reads it only from managed settings so that a user, project, or local file can't point the sandbox at a different binary.
settings.type: string, an absolute path; Claude Code drops a relative path and falls back to PATH lookup
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code finds bwrap on PATH

description.en: Point the sandbox at a bubblewrap binary installed outside PATH, such as a vendored copy on an air-gapped host. Claude Code uses the path both for the startup dependency check and when it wraps each sandboxed command.
description.zh: Point the sandbox at a bubblewrap binary installed outside PATH, such as a vendored copy on an air-gapped host. Claude Code uses the path both for the startup dependency check and when it wraps each sandboxed command.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code honors mask entries, allowPlaintextInject, awsPairs, and sigv4 only from user settings, managed settings, and the --settings flag.
settings.type: object with files, envVars, allowPlaintextInject, awsPairs, and sigv4
settings.default: unset, so no credentials are protected

description.en: Declare the credential files and environment variables to protect from sandboxed commands. Each entry names a file path or a variable name and a mode: deny hides the credential inside the sandbox, and mask shows sandboxed commands a placeholder while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests. Claude Code protects only the entries you list; there is no built-in credential deny list.
description.zh: Declare the credential files and environment variables to protect from sandboxed commands. Each entry names a file path or a variable name and a mode: deny hides the credential inside the sandbox, and mask shows sandboxed commands a placeholder while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests. Claude Code protects only the entries you list; there is no built-in credential deny list.

settings.default: false

description.en: Allow mask substitution on plain HTTP requests as well as TLS-terminated HTTPS. On plain HTTP the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext, so leave this off outside trusted test networks.
description.zh: Allow mask substitution on plain HTTP requests as well as TLS-terminated HTTPS. On plain HTTP the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext, so leave this off outside trusted test networks.

settings.type: array of objects, each with accessKeyIdVar, secretAccessKeyVar, and optionally sessionTokenVar, naming sandbox.credentials.envVars entries
settings.default: unset, so only the conventional trio is paired

description.en: Group masked environment variables that form one AWS credential for SigV4 re-signing when your credential lives in variables with non-standard names. Claude Code links the conventional AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN trio automatically when you mask their whole values, so you need this key only for other names. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
description.zh: Group masked environment variables that form one AWS credential for SigV4 re-signing when your credential lives in variables with non-standard names. Claude Code links the conventional AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN trio automatically when you mask their whole values, so you need this key only for other names. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code drops mask entries from project .claude/settings.json and local .claude/settings.local.json.
settings.type: array of objects, each with name and a mode of "deny" or "mask", plus the optional mask fields for environment variables
settings.default: unset, so no environment variables are protected

description.en: Protect environment variables from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code removes the variable from the environment of sandboxed commands. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands see a per-session sentinel value, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts, so tools such as gh and npm keep authenticating without ever holding the real credential.
description.zh: Protect environment variables from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code removes the variable from the environment of sandboxed commands. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands see a per-session sentinel value, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts, so tools such as gh and npm keep authenticating without ever holding the real credential.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code drops mask entries from project .claude/settings.json and local .claude/settings.local.json.
settings.type: array of objects, each with path and a mode of "deny" or "mask", plus the optional mask fields for files
settings.default: unset, so no credential files are protected

description.en: Protect credential files or directories from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code blocks reads of the path inside the sandbox, the same read block as sandbox.filesystem.denyRead. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands on Linux and WSL2 read a sentinel copy of the file, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts; on macOS the file is unreadable inside the sandbox instead. "mode": "mask" requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later.
description.zh: Protect credential files or directories from sandboxed commands. With "mode": "deny", Claude Code blocks reads of the path inside the sandbox, the same read block as sandbox.filesystem.denyRead. With "mode": "mask", sandboxed commands on Linux and WSL2 read a sentinel copy of the file, and the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to that entry's injectHosts; on macOS the file is unreadable inside the sandbox instead. "mode": "mask" requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later.

settings.type: object with streaming, presigned, and sigv4a, each one of:
settings.default: unset, so every form is "deny"

description.en: Choose what the sandbox proxy does with AWS request forms it can't re-sign: streaming for aws-chunked streaming uploads, presigned for presigned URLs, and sigv4a for SigV4A asymmetric signatures. This applies only to requests signed with a masked pair's placeholder access key ID. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
description.zh: Choose what the sandbox proxy does with AWS request forms it can't re-sign: streaming for aws-chunked streaming uploads, presigned for presigned URLs, and sigv4a for SigV4A asymmetric signatures. This applies only to requests signed with a masked pair's placeholder access key ID. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.default: false

description.en: Turn on sandboxing for Bash commands. When you pick a mode in the /sandbox panel, Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json for the current project; set it in ~/.claude/settings.json to sandbox every project.
description.zh: Turn on sandboxing for Bash commands. When you pick a mode in the /sandbox panel, Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json for the current project; set it in ~/.claude/settings.json to sandbox every project.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.default: false

description.en: Run the Linux sandbox inside an unprivileged Docker container, where bubblewrap can't mount a fresh /proc. Instead the inner sandbox bind-mounts the container's existing /proc, which exposes process information that a fresh mount would hide. This reduces security; use it only when the outer container already provides the isolation you need.
description.zh: Run the Linux sandbox inside an unprivileged Docker container, where bubblewrap can't mount a fresh /proc. Instead the inner sandbox bind-mounts the container's existing /proc, which exposes process information that a fresh mount would hide. This reduces security; use it only when the outer container already provides the isolation you need.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.default: false

description.en: Let sandboxed commands on macOS reach the system TLS trust service, com.apple.trustd.agent. Go-based tools such as gh, gcloud, and terraform need it to verify TLS certificates when you use network.httpProxyPort with a MITM proxy and a custom CA. This reduces security by opening a potential data exfiltration path through the trust service.
description.zh: Let sandboxed commands on macOS reach the system TLS trust service, com.apple.trustd.agent. Go-based tools such as gh, gcloud, and terraform need it to verify TLS certificates when you use network.httpProxyPort with a MITM proxy and a custom CA. This reduces security by opening a potential data exfiltration path through the trust service.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.default: unset, so no command is excluded

description.en: Name commands that Claude Code runs outside the sandbox, such as tools that don't work under it. Each entry uses the same syntax as the content of a Bash(...) permission rule: an exact command, a prefix such as docker *, or a wildcard pattern. A pattern with no wildcard is an exact match, so docker matches only docker with no arguments.
description.zh: Name commands that Claude Code runs outside the sandbox, such as tools that don't work under it. Each entry uses the same syntax as the content of a Bash(...) permission rule: an exact command, a prefix such as docker *, or a wildcard pattern. A pattern with no wildcard is an exact match, so docker matches only docker with no arguments.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.default: false

description.en: Make Claude Code exit with an error at startup when sandbox.enabled is true but the sandbox can't start, because a dependency is missing or the platform is unsupported. Without this key, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed. Managed deployments that require sandboxing as a security gate can use this setting.
description.zh: Make Claude Code exit with an error at startup when sandbox.enabled is true but the sandbox can't start, because a dependency is missing or the platform is unsupported. Without this key, Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed. Managed deployments that require sandboxing as a security gate can use this setting.

settings.type: object with allowWrite, denyWrite, denyRead, and allowRead arrays, plus the allowManagedReadPathsOnly and disabled Booleans
settings.default: unset, so the default read and write boundaries apply

description.en: Control which paths sandboxed commands can read and write. By default they can write to the working directory, the per-user temp directory, and directories you add with --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories, and can read the rest of the filesystem, including credential files. Widen or narrow that with the four path lists, or switch the filesystem layer off with disabled. See Filesystem isolation for the default boundaries.
description.zh: Control which paths sandboxed commands can read and write. By default they can write to the working directory, the per-user temp directory, and directories you add with --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories, and can read the rest of the filesystem, including credential files. Widen or narrow that with the four path lists, or switch the filesystem layer off with disabled. See Filesystem isolation for the default boundaries.

settings.default: false

description.en: Honor only the allowRead entries that come from managed settings, so developers can't re-open read access to paths your organization blocked. Claude Code still merges denyRead entries from every settings scope the session loads.
description.zh: Honor only the allowRead entries that come from managed settings, so developers can't re-open read access to paths your organization blocked. Claude Code still merges denyRead entries from every settings scope the session loads.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes
settings.default: unset

description.en: Re-open reading for specific paths inside a region that denyRead blocks, to build workspace-only read access. An exact or wildcard denyRead entry stays blocked inside a broader allowRead, as the overlap table shows. When a wildcard denyRead entry such as ~/**/.env matches a directory, Claude Code blocks reads of its contents as well. Before v2.1.236 on macOS, Claude Code re-opened the paths a wildcard denyRead entry matched wherever a broader allowRead entry covered them, and left a matched directory's contents readable.
description.zh: Re-open reading for specific paths inside a region that denyRead blocks, to build workspace-only read access. An exact or wildcard denyRead entry stays blocked inside a broader allowRead, as the overlap table shows. When a wildcard denyRead entry such as ~/**/.env matches a directory, Claude Code blocks reads of its contents as well. Before v2.1.236 on macOS, Claude Code re-opened the paths a wildcard denyRead entry matched wherever a broader allowRead entry covered them, and left a matched directory's contents readable.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes
settings.default: unset, so sandboxed commands can write to the working directory, the per-user temp directory, directories you've added with --add-dir or /add-dir, and directories in permissions.additionalDirectories

description.en: Add paths where sandboxed commands can write, beyond the working directory, the per-user temp directory, and the directories you've added with --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories. Use it when a subprocess such as kubectl or a build tool needs to write outside the project.
description.zh: Add paths where sandboxed commands can write, beyond the working directory, the per-user temp directory, and the directories you've added with --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories. Use it when a subprocess such as kubectl or a build tool needs to write outside the project.

settings.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes
settings.default: unset, so sandboxed commands keep the default read access, which includes credential files such as ~/.aws/credentials

description.en: Block sandboxed commands from reading specific paths, such as credential files that the default read policy would otherwise expose. To protect a credential file and keep it usable through the sandbox proxy, see sandbox.credentials instead.
description.zh: Block sandboxed commands from reading specific paths, such as credential files that the default read policy would otherwise expose. To protect a credential file and keep it usable through the sandbox proxy, see sandbox.credentials instead.

settings.type: array of path strings, using the sandbox path prefixes
settings.default: unset

description.en: Block sandboxed commands from writing to specific paths, including paths inside a directory that is otherwise writable.
description.zh: Block sandboxed commands from writing to specific paths, including paths inside a directory that is otherwise writable.

settings.scope: User or managed. When managed settings configure sandbox.filesystem at all, or list a sandbox.credentials.files entry with "mode": "deny", only managed settings can set it.
settings.default: false, so filesystem isolation stays on

description.en: Skip filesystem isolation while keeping network isolation. Sandboxed commands get unrestricted read and write access to the host filesystem, and their network egress stays confined to network.allowedDomains. Use it when you sandbox to control where commands connect rather than what they write. Requires Claude Code v2.1.216 or later.
description.zh: Skip filesystem isolation while keeping network isolation. Sandboxed commands get unrestricted read and write access to the host filesystem, and their network egress stays confined to network.allowedDomains. Use it when you sandbox to control where commands connect rather than what they write. Requires Claude Code v2.1.216 or later.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.type: object mapping a command substring to an array of violation substrings, usually paths
settings.default: unset, so every violation is reported

description.en: Silence sandbox violation reports for paths you expect a command to probe and be refused, such as a tool that checks /etc/hosts on startup, so those denials don't show up as violations or in what Claude sees. The sandbox still blocks the access; only the report is suppressed. Keys are substrings to match against the command, with * matching every command, and values are substrings of the violation to ignore for that command, such as a filesystem path.
description.zh: Silence sandbox violation reports for paths you expect a command to probe and be refused, such as a tool that checks /etc/hosts on startup, so those denials don't show up as violations or in what Claude sees. The sandbox still blocks the access; only the report is suppressed. Keys are substrings to match against the command, with * matching every command, and values are substrings of the violation to ignore for that command, such as a filesystem path.

settings.scope: Any file. strictAllowlist, allowManagedDomainsOnly, and tlsTerminate are read from fewer sources, as their entries say.
settings.default: unset, so no domains are pre-allowed and your permission mode decides what happens to each new host

description.en: Control which hosts, ports, and sockets sandboxed commands can reach. The sandbox routes outbound traffic through a proxy that enforces these lists; see Network isolation for how the proxy decides and when it prompts.
description.zh: Control which hosts, ports, and sockets sandboxed commands can reach. The sandbox routes outbound traffic through a proxy that enforces these lists; see Network isolation for how the proxy decides and when it prompts.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.default: false

description.en: Let sandboxed commands connect to every Unix socket. On Linux and WSL2, the sandbox's seccomp filter blocks socket(AF_UNIX, ...) calls, so this is the only way to permit Unix sockets there. When the filter is missing, which /sandbox reports on its Dependencies tab, the sandbox doesn't block Unix-socket calls. See Set up Linux and WSL2 for where the filter comes from.
description.zh: Let sandboxed commands connect to every Unix socket. On Linux and WSL2, the sandbox's seccomp filter blocks socket(AF_UNIX, ...) calls, so this is the only way to permit Unix sockets there. When the filter is missing, which /sandbox reports on its Dependencies tab, the sandbox doesn't block Unix-socket calls. See Set up Linux and WSL2 for where the filter comes from.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings. Only managed settings when allowManagedDomainsOnly is set.
settings.type: array of strings, each a domain, wildcard pattern, or IP literal, with an optional :port suffix
settings.default: unset, so your permission mode decides what happens to each new host

description.en: Pre-allow domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, so the sandbox doesn't prompt for them. Wildcards such as *.example.com match subdomains, and an optional :port suffix limits an entry to one port; an entry without a port matches every port.
description.zh: Pre-allow domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, so the sandbox doesn't prompt for them. Wildcards such as *.example.com match subdomains, and an optional :port suffix limits an entry to one port; an entry without a port matches every port.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.default: false

description.en: Let sandboxed commands on macOS listen on network ports, for example to start a dev server, and connect to any port on localhost. A command that listens on a non-loopback address accepts connections from other machines. The key has no effect on Linux and WSL2, where each sandboxed command has its own loopback interface. To reach a server on the host from Linux or WSL2, see A command fails to reach a server on localhost.
description.zh: Let sandboxed commands on macOS listen on network ports, for example to start a dev server, and connect to any port on localhost. A command that listens on a non-loopback address accepts connections from other machines. The key has no effect on Linux and WSL2, where each sandboxed command has its own loopback interface. To reach a server on the host from Linux or WSL2, see A command fails to reach a server on localhost.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.type: array of strings, each a service name; a single trailing matches a prefix, and "" alone matches every service
settings.default: unset

description.en: List additional XPC and Mach service names the macOS sandbox may look up. Tools that communicate over XPC, such as the iOS Simulator or Playwright, need their services listed here.
description.zh: List additional XPC and Mach service names the macOS sandbox may look up. Tools that communicate over XPC, such as the iOS Simulator or Playwright, need their services listed here.

settings.default: false

description.en: Lock the network allowlist to what managed settings define. Claude Code then honors only allowedDomains and WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules from managed settings, ignores domains from user, project, local, and --settings settings, and blocks a non-allowed domain automatically instead of prompting.
description.zh: Lock the network allowlist to what managed settings define. Claude Code then honors only allowedDomains and WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules from managed settings, ignores domains from user, project, local, and --settings settings, and blocks a non-allowed domain automatically instead of prompting.

settings.scope: Any file, with limits on project and local settings
settings.type: array of strings, each a socket path
settings.default: unset, so the macOS sandbox blocks every Unix socket

description.en: List the Unix socket paths sandboxed commands can connect to on macOS. Claude Code ignores this list on Linux and WSL2, where the seccomp filter can't inspect socket paths; use allowAllUnixSockets there instead.
description.zh: List the Unix socket paths sandboxed commands can connect to on macOS. Claude Code ignores this list on Linux and WSL2, where the seccomp filter can't inspect socket paths; use allowAllUnixSockets there instead.

settings.type: array of strings, each a domain, wildcard pattern, or IP literal, with an optional :port suffix
settings.default: unset

description.en: Block domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, using the same wildcard, port, and IPv6 syntax as allowedDomains. A denied domain stays blocked even when an allowedDomains entry matches it too.
description.zh: Block domains for outbound traffic from sandboxed commands, using the same wildcard, port, and IPv6 syntax as allowedDomains. A denied domain stays blocked even when an allowedDomains entry matches it too.

settings.scope: Any file, unless other sandbox settings limit which files can set a port
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code runs its own proxy

description.en: Point the sandbox at your own HTTP proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. Organizations do this to inspect HTTPS traffic, apply their own filtering rules, or log requests. Your proxy takes over filtering, and Claude Code stops applying its domain lists and network prompts to traffic sent there. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for HTTP traffic.
description.zh: Point the sandbox at your own HTTP proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. Organizations do this to inspect HTTPS traffic, apply their own filtering rules, or log requests. Your proxy takes over filtering, and Claude Code stops applying its domain lists and network prompts to traffic sent there. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for HTTP traffic.

settings.scope: Any file, unless other sandbox settings limit which files can set a port
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code runs its own proxy

description.en: Point the sandbox at your own SOCKS5 proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. Your proxy takes over filtering, and Claude Code stops applying its domain lists and network prompts to traffic sent there. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for SOCKS traffic.
description.zh: Point the sandbox at your own SOCKS5 proxy instead of the one Claude Code runs. Your proxy takes over filtering, and Claude Code stops applying its domain lists and network prompts to traffic sent there. When unset, Claude Code starts its own proxy for SOCKS traffic.

settings.scope: User or managed. A repository can't turn it on or off.
settings.default: false

description.en: Deny sandboxed commands access to hosts outside the allowlist instead of prompting for approval. The allowlist is allowedDomains plus domains from WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules, or only the managed settings entries when allowManagedDomainsOnly is set. Locks that apply without an admin-required sandbox covers a repository's entries. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.
description.zh: Deny sandboxed commands access to hosts outside the allowlist instead of prompting for approval. The allowlist is allowedDomains plus domains from WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules, or only the managed settings entries when allowManagedDomainsOnly is set. Locks that apply without an admin-required sandbox covers a repository's entries. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.

settings.scope: User or managed. A repository can't switch it on or supply a certificate authority.
settings.type: object with optional caCertPath and caKeyPath strings, each a file path
settings.default: unset, so the proxy doesn't terminate or inspect TLS

description.en: Make the sandbox proxy terminate TLS so it can read the contents of HTTPS requests. This is experimental, and mask credential substitution requires it. Set {} to generate an ephemeral certificate authority for the session, or set caCertPath and caKeyPath to use your own.
description.zh: Make the sandbox proxy terminate TLS so it can read the contents of HTTPS requests. This is experimental, and mask credential substitution requires it. Set {} to generate an ephemeral certificate authority for the session, or set caCertPath and caKeyPath to use your own.

settings.type: object with command, the path to the ripgrep binary, and optional args, an array of arguments to prepend
settings.default: unset, so the sandbox uses the same ripgrep binary as Claude Code. That is the bundled binary unless you set USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP to 0

description.en: Point the sandbox at a ripgrep binary of your own instead of the one Claude Code uses, for example when your platform needs a differently built rg.
description.zh: Point the sandbox at a ripgrep binary of your own instead of the one Claude Code uses, for example when your platform needs a differently built rg.

settings.type: string, an absolute path; Claude Code drops a relative path and falls back to PATH lookup
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code finds socat on PATH

description.en: Point the sandbox network proxy at a socat binary installed outside PATH.
description.zh: Point the sandbox network proxy at a socat binary installed outside PATH.

settings.default: false

description.en: When Claude finishes a plan in plan mode, it shows an approval menu. Planning can use a lot of context, so this key adds a first option to that menu, Yes, clear context and …, that approves the plan, clears the conversation context, and starts implementing from the plan alone. The rest of the label names the permission mode the session continues in, and shows how much of your context the planning used.
description.zh: When Claude finishes a plan in plan mode, it shows an approval menu. Planning can use a lot of context, so this key adds a first option to that menu, Yes, clear context and …, that approves the plan, clears the conversation context, and starts implementing from the plan alone. The rest of the label names the permission mode the session continues in, and shows how much of your context the planning used.

settings.default: false

description.en: See summaries of Claude's extended thinking in interactive sessions. Set it if you want the full summaries when you expand thinking with Ctrl+O. When unset or false, the Anthropic API redacts thinking blocks and Claude Code shows a collapsed stub; third-party providers don't redact.
description.zh: See summaries of Claude's extended thinking in interactive sessions. Set it if you want the full summaries when you expand thinking with Ctrl+O. When unset or false, the Anthropic API redacts thinking blocks and Claude Code shows a collapsed stub; third-party providers don't redact.

settings.scope: Any file. A value in ~/.claude.json from an older version applies when no settings file sets it.
settings.default: true

description.en: Show or hide the turn duration message after each response, such as "Cooked for 1m 6s · done 6:05 PM". The clock after "done" shows when the turn finished; timeFormat and timeZone control its format and zone. Appears in /config as Show turn duration.
description.zh: Show or hide the turn duration message after each response, such as "Cooked for 1m 6s · done 6:05 PM". The clock after "done" shows when the turn finished; timeFormat and timeZone control its format and zone. Appears in /config as Show turn duration.

settings.type: number, a fraction greater than 0 and at most 1
settings.default: 0.01, which reserves 1% of the context window

description.en: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills with their descriptions, and Claude Code caps that listing at a share of the context window. When the listing is over the cap, Claude Code keeps every skill's name but drops the descriptions of the least-used skills, so Claude can still invoke those skills but is less likely to choose one on its own. Raise this key to keep more descriptions visible at the cost of more context per turn.
description.zh: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills with their descriptions, and Claude Code caps that listing at a share of the context window. When the listing is over the cap, Claude Code keeps every skill's name but drops the descriptions of the least-used skills, so Claude can still invoke those skills but is less likely to choose one on its own. Raise this key to keep more descriptions visible at the cost of more context per turn.

settings.type: number of characters, a positive integer

description.en: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills that shows each skill's description and when_to_use text. This key caps how many characters of that text Claude Code shows per skill; longer text is cut at the cap.
description.zh: Each turn, Claude sees a listing of your skills that shows each skill's description and when_to_use text. This key caps how many characters of that text Claude Code shows per skill; longer text is cut at the cap.

settings.scope: Any file. The /skills menu writes to .claude/settings.local.json.
settings.type: object mapping skill name to one of:
settings.default: unset, so every skill is "on"

description.en: Hide or collapse a skill without editing its SKILL.md. Claude Code applies the value under each skill's name to the skill list Claude sees and to your / autocomplete.
description.zh: Hide or collapse a skill without editing its SKILL.md. Claude Code applies the value under each skill's name to the skill list Claude sees and to your / autocomplete.

settings.scope: User or managed. A repository can't set it for you.
settings.default: unset, so the notice appears once

description.en: Skip the one-time notice describing auto mode that Claude Code shows when you first enter auto mode yourself, for example through your own settings or the mode selector, rather than when the built-in default starts a session in it. Claude Code shows that notice once and then records that it was shown, so this key only matters where the notice hasn't appeared yet.
description.zh: Skip the one-time notice describing auto mode that Claude Code shows when you first enter auto mode yourself, for example through your own settings or the mode selector, rather than when the built-in default starts a session in it. Claude Code shows that notice once and then records that it was shown, so this key only matters where the notice hasn't appeared yet.

settings.scope: User, local, or managed. An untrusted repository can't skip the dialog for you.
settings.default: unset, so the dialog appears

description.en: Skip the confirmation dialog Claude Code shows before a session enters bypassPermissions mode, whether from --dangerously-skip-permissions or from defaultMode: "bypassPermissions". Claude Code writes true here in your user settings when you accept that dialog once.
description.zh: Skip the confirmation dialog Claude Code shows before a session enters bypassPermissions mode, whether from --dangerously-skip-permissions or from defaultMode: "bypassPermissions". Claude Code writes true here in your user settings when you accept that dialog once.

settings.default: unset, so the check runs before the first fetch to each hostname in a session

description.en: Skip the WebFetch domain safety check, which sends each requested hostname to api.anthropic.com before fetching. Set true in environments that block traffic to Anthropic, such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry deployments with restrictive egress.
description.zh: Skip the WebFetch domain safety check, which sends each requested hostname to api.anthropic.com before fetching. Set true in environments that block traffic to Anthropic, such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry deployments with restrictive egress.

settings.scope: User or managed. The block from the highest tier that sets it applies as a whole.
settings.type: object with enabled (Boolean), checker ("aspell", "hunspell", "ispell", or "auto"), language (string, passed to the checker as its dictionary name), and color (string, a terminal color name, #rrggbb, rgb(r,g,b), ansi256(n), or ansi:)
settings.default: unset, so spell checking is off; checker defaults to "auto", the first of the three found on PATH; language defaults to the checker's own dictionary; color defaults to the theme's error color

description.en: Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using a spell checker you install. Claude Code checks only the text in the input box. Check spelling as you type covers installing aspell, hunspell, or ispell and what the checker covers. Requires Claude Code v2.1.235 or later.
description.zh: Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using a spell checker you install. Claude Code checks only the text in the input box. Check spelling as you type covers installing aspell, hunspell, or ispell and what the checker covers. Requires Claude Code v2.1.235 or later.

settings.default: true

description.en: While Claude works, the spinner line rotates through short tips about Claude Code features, such as "Use Plan Mode to prepare for a complex request before making changes. Press Shift+Tab twice to enable." Set this key to false to hide them. Appears in /config as Show tips.
description.zh: While Claude works, the spinner line rotates through short tips about Claude Code features, such as "Use Plan Mode to prepare for a complex request before making changes. Press Shift+Tab twice to enable." Set this key to false to hide them. Appears in /config as Show tips.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code honors tip objects, tipsFile, label, and excludeDefault from user settings, the --settings flag, and managed settings; from project and local settings it reads plain string tips only.
settings.type: object with tips, tipsFile, label, and excludeDefault fields, each optional
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code shows only the built-in tips

description.en: Add your own tips to the spinner tips that Claude Code shows while Claude works, or replace the built-in tips with yours. Claude Code puts your tips in the same rotation as the built-in ones.
description.zh: Add your own tips to the spinner tips that Claude Code shows while Claude works, or replace the built-in tips with yours. Claude Code puts your tips in the same rotation as the built-in ones.

settings.type: object with a verbs array of strings and mode, one of:
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the built-in verbs

description.en: While a turn is in progress, the spinner shows a rotating verb such as "Accomplishing", "Architecting", or "Baking". Use this key to add your own verbs to that rotation or replace the built-in list with yours.
description.zh: While a turn is in progress, the spinner shows a rotating verb such as "Accomplishing", "Architecting", or "Baking". Use this key to add your own verbs to that rotation or replace the built-in list with yours.

settings.scope: User or managed. The desktop app reads this key. By default, it reads managed connections from one managed source.
settings.type: array of objects, each with required id, name, and sshHost and optional sshPort and sshIdentityFile
settings.default: unset

description.en: Add SSH connections to the Desktop environment dropdown. Administrators use it to distribute shared connections to a team. Connections you define in managed settings show as managed, so users can select them but can't edit or delete them in the app.
description.zh: Add SSH connections to the Desktop environment dropdown. Administrators use it to distribute shared connections to a team. Connections you define in managed settings show as managed, so users can select them but can't edit or delete them in the app.

settings.scope: Managed. By default, Desktop reads the key from one managed source.
settings.default: unset, so any host is allowed

description.en: Limit the hosts a Desktop SSH session can connect to. Only the Desktop app reads this key; the CLI doesn't. Patterns are case-insensitive: matches any host, .example.com matches example.com and every subdomain, and anything else is an exact match against the hostname after ~/.ssh/config resolution. An empty array turns SSH sessions off.
description.zh: Limit the hosts a Desktop SSH session can connect to. Only the Desktop app reads this key; the CLI doesn't. Patterns are case-insensitive: matches any host, .example.com matches example.com and every subdomain, and anything else is an exact match against the hostname after ~/.ssh/config resolution. An empty array turns SSH sessions off.

settings.scope: Any file. When allowManagedHooksOnly is on, or disableAllHooks is set outside managed settings, only the managed settings value runs.
settings.type: object with type set to "command" and a command string, plus optional padding as a number of characters, refreshInterval as a number of seconds, minimum 1, and hideVimModeIndicator as a Boolean
settings.default: unset, so no status line

description.en: Run your own command to render a status line below the prompt with context such as the model, cost, or git branch. Optional fields adjust spacing, add periodic re-runs, and hide the built-in vim mode indicator when your script renders vim.mode itself.
description.zh: Run your own command to render a status line below the prompt with context such as the model, cost, or git branch. Optional fields adjust spacing, add periodic re-runs, and hide the built-in vim mode indicator when your script renders vim.mode itself.

settings.type: array of marketplace source objects; see Allowed source types
settings.default: unset, so users can add any marketplace. An empty array is a complete lockdown that blocks every marketplace source, including the official Anthropic marketplace

description.en: Restrict which plugin marketplace sources people in your organization can add and install plugins from. Claude Code enforces the allowlist on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, before any network or filesystem operation, so a marketplace someone added before you set the policy can't be used to fetch plugins once its source no longer matches. Blocked users see an error naming the managed policy.
description.zh: Restrict which plugin marketplace sources people in your organization can add and install plugins from. Claude Code enforces the allowlist on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, before any network or filesystem operation, so a marketplace someone added before you set the policy can't be used to fetch plugins once its source no longer matches. Blocked users see an error naming the managed policy.

settings.type: true to lock all four kinds of customization, or an array naming the kinds to lock, from "skills", "agents", "hooks", and "mcp"
settings.default: unset, so nothing is locked

description.en: Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can come only from plugins or managed settings. Combine it with strictKnownMarketplaces to control the full customization supply chain: the marketplace allowlist controls which plugins users can install.
description.zh: Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can come only from plugins or managed settings. Combine it with strictKnownMarketplaces to control the full customization supply chain: the marketplace allowlist controls which plugins users can install.

settings.type: the string "agents" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array
settings.default: not locked

description.en: Lock the agents surface. Claude Code stops loading agents from ~/.claude/agents/, .claude/agents/, and --add-dir directories. It keeps loading plugin agents, built-in agents, and agents in the managed policy directory.
description.zh: Lock the agents surface. Claude Code stops loading agents from ~/.claude/agents/, .claude/agents/, and --add-dir directories. It keeps loading plugin agents, built-in agents, and agents in the managed policy directory.

settings.type: the string "hooks" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array
settings.default: not locked

description.en: Lock the hooks surface. Claude Code stops running hooks from user, project, and local settings.json, and keeps running plugin hooks and hooks in managed settings.
description.zh: Lock the hooks surface. Claude Code stops running hooks from user, project, and local settings.json, and keeps running plugin hooks and hooks in managed settings.

settings.type: the string "mcp" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array
settings.default: not locked

description.en: Lock the mcp surface. Claude Code stops loading MCP servers from ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json, and keeps loading plugin MCP servers, managed-mcp.json servers, and servers from managedMcpServers.
description.zh: Lock the mcp surface. Claude Code stops loading MCP servers from ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json, and keeps loading plugin MCP servers, managed-mcp.json servers, and servers from managedMcpServers.

settings.type: the string "skills" in the strictPluginOnlyCustomization array
settings.default: not locked

description.en: Lock the skills surface. Claude Code stops loading skills from ~/.claude/skills/ and .claude/skills/, custom commands from ~/.claude/commands/ and .claude/commands/, skills and commands under --add-dir directories, and skills synced from your claude.ai account. It keeps loading plugin skills, bundled skills, and skills in the managed policy directory.
description.zh: Lock the skills surface. Claude Code stops loading skills from ~/.claude/skills/ and .claude/skills/, custom commands from ~/.claude/commands/ and .claude/commands/, skills and commands under --add-dir directories, and skills synced from your claude.ai account. It keeps loading plugin skills, bundled skills, and skills in the managed policy directory.

settings.default: unset, so each of these requests gets its default lifetime

description.en: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the requests Claude Code makes outside the main conversation. This key applies to subagents, workflows, and Claude Code's own background and helper requests, such as compaction and session titles. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks, and the API bills each cache write at a higher rate than at the five-minute lifetime. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.
description.zh: Choose how long the prompt cache holds the requests Claude Code makes outside the main conversation. This key applies to subagents, workflows, and Claude Code's own background and helper requests, such as compaction and session titles.
